title: Gateway to the Americas Bridge to halt northbound traffic early Nov. 17 and Nov. 19
excerpt: Northbound vehicle and pedestrian traffic at the Gateway to the Americas Bridge will be halted from 2 to 4 a.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 17, and Thursday, Nov. 19, for facility upgrades, with the Juarez-Lincoln Bridge as the alternate route.
content:
Northbound vehicle and pedestrian traffic at the Gateway to the Americas Bridge will be temporarily halted in the early morning hours of Tuesday, Nov. 17, and Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, from 2:00 to 4:00 a.m., for essential facility upgrades, according to U.S. Customs and Border Protection.

Traffic is expected to resume at approximately 4:00 a.m. on both mornings, CBP said.

CBP is encouraging travelers who plan to use the bridge during those hours to make prior arrangements. Drivers who need to cross while the halt is in effect can use the Juarez-Lincoln Bridge as an alternative route, according to the agency.

CBP also reminded travelers to carry radio frequency identification (RFID) document-equipped travel documents and have them ready when entering the United States through designated Ready Lanes. Travelers can check border wait times through CBP's Border Wait Times page or the BWT app, which updates hourly.

Sources: U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Nov. 10, 2026; TheTrucker.com, Nov. 11, 2026.
